title: Client runtime contracts: resumable streams, cursor semantics, retry strategy, and compatibility
creator: Leah Park
description: PRD for a consistent client-side contract across Python/TS/Go SDKs that standardizes resumable streaming behavior, cursor semantics for paginated endpoints, and retry/idempotency expectations. Goal: reduce production incidents caused by divergent SDK semantics, enable graceful server-side rollout of streaming resume, and make client upgrades low-friction for customers.
scope: In scope: design and acceptance criteria for resumable LLM streams (resume token format, retention window, client reconnection behavior), canonical cursor semantics for paginated APIs (opaque cursor lifecycle, TTL, stable ordering requirements), and a retry strategy (idempotency keys, retry budget, backoff defaults). Implementation of SDK helpers and cross-language examples (Python/TS/Go) and integration test matrix. Out of scope: deep server-side storage design, telemetry ingestion pipeline changes (will be covered by infra).
non_goals: Do not change existing public endpoint names; do not require customers to change prompts or prompt state. Not changing model semantics or output shape beyond the minimal resume metadata envelope. Not implementing custom transport layers beyond the SDK wrappers.
requirements: 1) Resumable streaming: server returns an opaque resume_token at safe points in the stream; SDKs must persist token atomically alongside any local buffered output. On reconnect, SDK provides token and server will resume from the last server-acknowledged token. 2) Resume token format: short, base64url encoded blob with version prefix (v1: runtime-v1), max 1KB, and server-side TTL currently 5 minutes (configurable). 3) Client reconnection policy: first immediate reconnect, then exponential backoff up to 30s; surface a "resumed" event to caller when resume succeeds and a clear error when resume fails. 4) Idempotency and retries: all non-streaming mutating calls must accept an idempotency_key; SDK will generate RFC4122 v4 by default but expose override. Retry budget: default 3 attempts for 5xx/network errors with jittered exponential backoff; do not retry on 4xx except 429 with Retry-After respect. 5) Pagination/cursor: cursors are opaque strings returned under `next_cursor`; cursor invalidation returns 410 with guidance; SDKs must expose iterator helpers that swallow transient resume/retry under the hood while allowing manual control. 6) Backpressure and buffering: SDKs will expose a streaming iterator abstraction that supports a high-water mark and provides a cancel() method to release server resources. 7) Compatibility modes: SDKs must provide a "compatibility" flag to enable legacy behavior (current pre-change semantics) for at least two SDK minor versions to ease customer migration.
language_specific_examples: Python: Streaming client returns a `ResumableStream` object with `.resume_token`, `.persist_token(callback)`, and async iterator semantics; example shows try/except with auto-reconnect. TS: Browser and Node variants; Node uses an event emitter and exposes `persistResumeToken()` that accepts a user-provided storage adapter (localStorage/File). Go: idiomatic `io.Reader`-style stream with `Resume()` method returning error semantics; provide helper for context-aware reconnect. Each SDK example includes snippet showing idempotency_key injection and iterator usage for pagination.
api_contract_changes: Server adds optional response envelope fields: `resume_token` (string), `resume_point` (human-readable progress hint), and `cursor_ttl_seconds` for paginated endpoints. Servers may start returning these gradually behind a feature flag. The public REST/WebSocket surface remains the same; the new fields are additive. SDKs must gracefully ignore unknown new envelope fields and allow opt-in for strict validation. Servers will add 410 for expired cursor and 409 for resume conflicts with clear machine-readable error codes.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python, TS, Go) include implemented helpers for resumable streaming with at least one integration test each: successful resume within TTL and failure path when TTL expired.
Pagination iterator helpers present and tested to: follow `next_cursor`, surface 410 cursor-expired errors with a documented recovery path, and preserve ordering guarantees in integration tests.
Retry behavior benchmarked in unit tests: default 3 retries for transient 5xx with exponential backoff; 429 honors Retry-After header; SDK exposes configuration overrides.
Compatibility flag in each SDK that toggles legacy behavior; documented migration guide and compatibility matrix stating which minor versions support the flag.
End-to-end interop test harness demonstrating server feature-flag rollout + client compat flag: server toggled to send resume_token, SDK persists and uses it successfully in canary run.
Clear public changelog entries and code samples in the SDK docs for streaming resume and cursor migration.
Telemetry events emitted: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure, cursor_expired — verified by e2e test using a mock telemetry sink.
SDK maintainers have signed off in GH PRs and PM has approved documentation before release.
Performance: added resume semantics do not increase median latency for cold-stream start by more than 5% in internal perf tests.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (server): implement feature-flagged resume_token on a small percentage of traffic and enable debug telemetry. Phase 2 (SDK alpha): ship SDK alpha with opt-in `compatibility=false` default for early adopters; collect crash/telemetry. Phase 3 (SDK stable): turn on resume by default with compatibility flag available; support customer rollback by setting compatibility=true. Phase 4: deprecate compatibility flag after two minor releases and announce migration schedule. Canary groups prioritized by customer tier and opt-in list.
migration_notes: For customers persisting cursors in their DBs: validate that stored cursor strings are treated as opaque; new server will return 410 when invalid — recommend treat 410 as signal to re-fetch first page and surface a UX to user. For streaming: provide code snippets to persist resume_token to durable storage atomically alongside any local transcript before acknowledging success to the host app.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: resume_token leak could expose metadata. Mitigation: tokens are opaque and short-lived; ensure tokens contain no plaintext PII and are HMACed server-side.
Risk: clients will persist tokens indefinitely. Mitigation: TTL enforcement + server returns clear 410; SDKs will leak a warning telemetry event when persisted token usage exceeds TTL window.

Risk: inconsistent ordering across paginated endpoints during rapid writes. Mitigation: enforce strong ordering on server for endpoints marked as "stable-order"; document endpoints without strong ordering and advise cursor use only for read-only traversal.
Risk: increased SDK complexity causing bugs. Mitigation: comprehensive unit + integration tests, code walkthroughs, and a short RFC reviewed by Eng + Security.

Risk: existing customers break on default behavior change. Mitigation: default to legacy behavior behind a compatibility flag for two releases and communicate proactively via release notes and account outreach for high-impact customers.
